title: Live Esports Broadcast Pipeline Atlas
description: A production-system map from gameplay and cameras through capture, scenes, audio, encoding, transport, platforms, viewers, monitoring and rights-aware archiving.

curriculumPresets.title: Full broadcast pipeline
curriculumPresets.description: Follow video, audio, data and control from sources to live viewers and archived content.

curriculumPresets.title: L2 Unit 3: streaming for esports
curriculumPresets.description: Build a simple one-PC or two-PC workflow, then justify capture, audio, scenes, encoder, platform and moderation choices.

curriculumPresets.title: L3 Unit 6: live-streamed broadcasting
curriculumPresets.description: Analyse hardware, software, platform functions, overlays, lower thirds, data, audio and legal or data-protection controls across a full production.

curriculumPresets.title: L3 Unit 20: networking
curriculumPresets.description: Focus on NDI, SRT, RTMP ingestion, HLS delivery, bitrate, latency, resilience and monitoring. Locate each protocol within the path.

curriculumPresets.title: Production troubleshooting
curriculumPresets.description: Start at the viewer symptom, work upstream through platform, transport, encoder, mixer and source, and record evidence before changing settings.

nodes.name: Live Broadcast System
nodes.note: A live stream is a chain of sources, capture, production, encoding, transport, distribution and audience feedback. Reliability is limited by the weakest stage.
nodes.hook: Choose one viewer symptom and trace every upstream component that could cause it.

nodes.name: 1. Sources
nodes.note: Gameplay, cameras, microphones and data enter the production as distinct signals with different timing and privacy risks.
nodes.hook: Create a source list including connector, format, owner and fallback.

nodes.name: Gameplay output
nodes.note: A game PC or console supplies programme video and game audio.
nodes.hook: Check resolution, refresh rate, colour range and copy-protection compatibility.

nodes.name: Cameras and webcams
nodes.note: Cameras add presenters, players, stage and venue context.
nodes.hook: Set framing, exposure and consent requirements before going live.

nodes.name: Microphones and comms
nodes.note: Commentary, presenters, game sound and communications need separate routing and monitoring.
nodes.hook: Make an audio patch list and prevent private comms reaching programme output.

nodes.name: Game and event data
nodes.note: Scores, names, clocks, statistics and bracket data drive graphics and commentary.
nodes.hook: Define who may edit each field and how an error is corrected on air.

nodes.name: 2. Capture and Ingest
nodes.note: Capture converts or transfers source signals into the production system.
nodes.hook: Compare one-PC, two-PC and network-video designs against budget and failure risk.

nodes.name: One-PC workflow
nodes.note: The game and production software share one computer’s resources.
nodes.hook: Measure game frame time and encoder load under realistic scenes.

nodes.name: HDMI capture card
nodes.note: A capture device ingests video from a console, camera or separate gaming PC.
nodes.hook: Check input, passthrough and USB/PCIe bandwidth against the required format.

nodes.name: Two-PC workflow
nodes.note: A gaming system sends audio/video to a dedicated production computer.
nodes.hook: Explain which failures are isolated and which new cables or routing risks appear.

nodes.name: NDI over IP
nodes.note: NDI transports video, audio and metadata across an IP network for production.
nodes.hook: Calculate whether the LAN and switches can support every planned stream.

nodes.name: 3. Production and Mixing
nodes.note: Production software and operators compose sources into a coherent programme.
nodes.hook: Turn a running order into scenes, cues, roles and contingencies.

nodes.name: OBS Studio
nodes.note: OBS captures and mixes real-time video and audio into scenes for recording and streaming.
nodes.hook: Build scenes with consistent naming and test every transition before broadcast.

nodes.name: Scenes and transitions
nodes.note: Scenes organise layouts such as holding, gameplay, desk, interview and results.
nodes.hook: Create a minimum scene set and explain the purpose of each.

nodes.name: Overlays and lower thirds
nodes.note: Graphics communicate identity, names, score, state and sponsorship without hiding critical play.
nodes.hook: Test legibility at phone size and against changing game backgrounds.

nodes.name: Audio mixing and monitoring
nodes.note: Level, routing, delay, filters and monitoring determine whether speech and game audio remain intelligible and synchronised.
nodes.hook: Use meters and headphones to set a repeatable speech-over-game balance.

nodes.name: Observer and replay
nodes.note: Observers select in-game viewpoints; replay operators recover important action.
nodes.hook: Prioritise information and narrative when several events happen simultaneously.

nodes.name: 4. Encoding
nodes.note: An encoder compresses programme video and audio within platform, hardware and bandwidth limits.
nodes.hook: Justify codec, resolution, frame rate, bitrate and keyframe interval as one connected choice.

nodes.name: Software encoding
nodes.note: CPU-based encoding shares general compute with production and other applications.
nodes.hook: Monitor utilisation and dropped frames during a stress test.

nodes.name: Hardware encoding
nodes.note: Dedicated media blocks can reduce CPU load, with quality and feature trade-offs.
nodes.hook: Compare output quality at equal bitrate using a moving gameplay sequence.

nodes.name: Multiple renditions
nodes.note: Multiple resolution and bitrate versions can improve viewer adaptation but increase encoding and upload demand.
nodes.hook: Create a bandwidth budget before enabling simultaneous encodes.

nodes.name: 5. Contribution Transport
nodes.note: Contribution protocols carry the encoded programme from production to a platform or remote production centre.
nodes.hook: Place each protocol on the path and avoid confusing contribution with viewer delivery.

nodes.name: RTMP / RTMPS ingest
nodes.note: RTMP and encrypted RTMPS remain common live-platform ingest protocols.
nodes.hook: Check platform server URL, stream-key security and firewall requirements.

nodes.name: SRT contribution
nodes.note: SRT is designed for secure, reliable, low-latency contribution across unpredictable networks.
nodes.hook: Test latency and packet loss while changing the recovery buffer.

nodes.name: Internet and redundancy
nodes.note: Upload capacity, stability, routing and backup connectivity determine contribution reliability.
nodes.hook: Measure sustained upload and define the trigger for switching to a backup path.

nodes.name: 6. Platform Distribution
nodes.note: Platforms ingest, process, moderate, transcode, package and distribute live content.
nodes.hook: Compare creator controls with platform-controlled processing.

nodes.name: Twitch
nodes.note: Twitch provides live distribution, chat and broadcast workflows, including enhanced multi-encode options.
nodes.hook: Configure a private test and document moderation plus failure-recovery controls.

nodes.name: YouTube Live
nodes.note: YouTube accepts encoder contribution and creates viewer-compatible output formats.
nodes.hook: Match official encoder settings to the event’s resolution and frame rate.

nodes.name: Platform transcoding
nodes.note: Platforms may create multiple renditions to suit different viewer connections and devices.
nodes.hook: Explain why the creator’s upload bitrate is not the viewer’s only option.

nodes.name: HLS delivery
nodes.note: HTTP Live Streaming segments and playlists support adaptive viewer delivery through ordinary web infrastructure.
nodes.hook: Trace manifest, media segments, CDN cache and player adaptation.

nodes.name: 7. Audience and Assurance
nodes.note: Viewer experience, moderation, analytics, monitoring and archiving close the production loop.
nodes.hook: Define quality indicators from both operator and viewer perspectives.

nodes.name: Viewer player and device
nodes.note: The player selects a rendition, buffers content and presents it under device and network constraints.
nodes.hook: Test the programme on mobile, desktop and a restricted connection.

nodes.name: Chat and moderation
nodes.note: Live interaction needs clear rules, moderation tools, escalation and safeguarding.
nodes.hook: Create a moderation matrix for spam, harassment, spoilers and safeguarding concerns.

nodes.name: Confidence monitoring
nodes.note: Operators should monitor local programme, platform return and public output because each proves a different stage.
nodes.hook: Match each monitoring point to the failures it can reveal.

nodes.name: Stream health and analytics
nodes.note: Dropped frames, bitrate, latency, playback failures and engagement metrics support technical and editorial review.
nodes.hook: Separate real-time fault indicators from post-event success measures.

nodes.name: Recording, rights and data
nodes.note: Recordings, music, player images, chat, names and analytics may create copyright, consent, retention and data-protection duties.
nodes.hook: Build a pre-flight rights and data checklist with named owners and retention periods.

edges.note: HDMI or similar output is ingested by the capture device.
Camera capture becomes a production source.
Microphone signals are routed and mixed.
Capture devices expose video and audio to production software.
NDI sources can enter IP-based production.
The mixed programme is passed to an encoder.
OBS can use supported hardware encoders.
Encoded output is sent using a contribution protocol.
Remote workflows may use SRT contribution.
RTMP/RTMPS can feed a live platform.
SRT may feed compatible platforms or remote production gateways.
Platform processing can create viewer renditions.
YouTube automatically processes live output formats.
Viewer renditions can be packaged for adaptive delivery.
The player retrieves playlists and media segments.
